content.comment_body: Dear forum members, the update to [product_name] [version_no] is now available online. Visit [url] for a free upgrade, or use the help/update center in [product_name] for the update.
[user_name] - Thanks for sharing. Can you provide a more direct download link for [product_name]?
Is there information available about the changes in this version?
No official changelog provided. Just use the link above, select 'Upgrades' (be careful not to download the demo version), choose your platform and operating system, and run the executable.
I currently have [version_no] installed. Is there a direct link for the update to [version_no], or do I need to complete the upgrade process from the older version?

Run [product_name] [version_no] as administrator and select Help > Update Center. Choose Internet as the update source, accept the suggested internet address, select the service pack for [version_no], and follow the instructions.
I found the changelog in the latest manual for [product_name] [version_no].

Hello, I downloaded [version_no] as follows: First, did nothing with the installed version. Second, accessed the download page (same link as above). Third, downloaded based on operating system and platform, including Java. No changelog was needed or requested. Now both versions—old and new—are installed on my PC, each with different language options. For language packs or service packs, use the Update Center in the Help menu of [product_name]. Note: I tried downloading a language pack but received an error message. I have contacted [company_name] for assistance, no response yet. More info at [url]

The online help for [product_name] [version_no] explains that all available language packs are now installed automatically, and no further updates are necessary—hence the error message when checking in the update center.

Hello, the main issue with language packs is that [version_no] does not offer the same options as earlier versions. Some language packs—such as Czech, Hungarian, and Portuguese—are no longer available. Waiting for confirmation from [company_name] regarding discontinued language support. The number of languages has decreased.
This situation existed with previous versions too—certain languages stopped being supported, such as Dutch in earlier updates.
It seems that the less common languages are provided for specific regions.
Do you have a reliable source for this? These languages aren't installed by default but are still needed by users. The Dutch language pack can be downloaded from the relevant regional site.

I don't require Dutch, just noting that not all language packs were available in past upgrades. For example, Dutch was missing in the update to [version_no]. Now, only German, English, Spanish, Italian, French, and Chinese are provided. Language packs from previous versions can't be installed on [version_no].
Is there an expected release date for the Polish language pack for [product_name] [version_no]?
Submit a support request to [company_name] for this issue.

A new question by [user_name] was split into a separate thread regarding an error ('Windows error 216 occurred while loading the Java VM') during upgrade. Is there a solution for this problem? Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users welcome the release of the [product_name] [version_no] upgrade, but express confusion about where to find changelogs and details about the update process, especially regarding changes in language pack availability. Reduced support for certain languages and unclear error messages when attempting to install additional language packs are the main user experience concerns.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a smooth upgrade process, clear and accessible documentation such as changelogs, and continued support for all previously available language packs.
